'''Vyjayanthi Chari''' (born 1958)<ref>Birth year from [http://www.isni.org/isni/0000000115646013 ISNI authority control file], accessed 2018-11-26.</ref> is an Indian–American Distinguished Professor and the F. Burton Jones Endowed Chair for Pure Mathematics at the [[University of California, Riverside]], known for her research in [[representation theory]] and [[quantum algebra]].<ref name="profile">{{citation|url=http://mathdept.ucr.edu/faculty/chari.html|title=Faculty profile|publisher=Department of Mathematics, University of California, Riverside|access-date=2015-11-17}}.</ref> In 2015 she was elected as a [[fellow]] of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.ams.org/profession/ams-fellows/new-fellows|title=2016 Class of the Fellows of the AMS|publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]]|access-date=2015-11-17|archive-date=2019-05-16|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190516101122/http://ams.org/profession/ams-fellows/new-fellows|url-status=dead}}.</ref>

== Education ==
Chari has a bachelor's, master's, and doctoral degree from the [[University of Mumbai]].<ref name="profile" /> Chari received her Ph.D. from the University of Mumbai under the supervision of  [[Rajagopalan Parthasarathy]].<ref name=":0">{{mathgenealogy|id=49988}}</ref>

== Professional career ==
Following her Ph.D., she became a fellow at the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research, Mumbai. In 1991, she joined the [[University of California, Riverside]] (UCR) where  she is now a Distinguished Professor of Mathematics. During her career, she has had several visiting positions. They were: invited senior participant at the Mittag-Leffler Institute, Sweden; an invited professor at the University of Cologne, Germany; an invited professor at Paris 7, France; an invited research fellow at Brown University, RI; and an invited senior participant at Hausdorff Research Institute for Mathematics, Bonn, Germany;  and visiting professor at the [[University of Rome Tor Vergata]], Italy.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://ucrtoday.ucr.edu/32891|title=Mathematician Named Fellow of American Mathematical Society |first1=Iqbal |last=Pittalwala |date=30 October 2015|website=UCR Today|language=en-US|access-date=2020-01-17}}</ref>

She is also the editor of the ''Pacific Journal of Mathematics'' and the Editor in Chief of ''Algebras and Representation Theory''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=UCR Profiles - Search & Browse |url=https://profiles.ucr.edu/app/home/profile/vyjayanc |access-date=2025-05-19 |website=profiles.ucr.edu}}</ref>

With Andrew N. Pressley, she is the author of the book ''A Guide to Quantum Groups'' (Cambridge University Press, 1994).<ref>Review of ''A Guide to Quantum Groups'' by Tomasz Brzeziński (1995), {{MR|1300632}}.</ref>

== Honors ==

* The Doctoral Dissertation Advisor/Mentor Award from the UCR Academic Senate.<ref name=":1" />
* American Mathematical Society 2016 Class of Fellows.
* Simons Fellow 2019–2020.
*Infosys Visiting Chair Professor, Indian Institute of Science, 2019–2023.
